thread:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 - GPUPool gpux-eu exhausted. Symptoms: queued requests >900, provider 429/503 mix, autoscaler showing repeated "CreateFailed" and "Timeout". Paging oncall @kai and infra @maria.

kai: acknowledging. joining call. quick ask: any recent infra deploys to pool config?
jordan: rolled out small autoscaler tuning 01:30 UTC that reduced aggressive retries. not expecting failure but sending the diff now.
sara: observed `inference_queue_length` spike at 02:48 UTC from ~50 -> 920 within 7 minutes. 99th latency spiking and customers getting error 429s.
maria: provider error stream shows quota/placement failures followed by image pull timeouts for some nodes. autoscaler tries to create instances but they repeatedly fail to reach Ready.
ops-bot: Automated mitigation suggestions: 1) enable burst-protection on pool 2) shift non-SLA traffic 3) increase per-tenant soft limit.

kai: execute ops-bot suggestions stepwise. First toggle burst-protection to shed low-priority requests.

```
# enable burst protection (infra)
infra modify-pool --pool gpux-eu --burst-protection true
```

jordan: toggled burst-protection. low-priority tenants now rate-limited. queue reduced ~20%.

sara: still seeing CreateFailed spikes. digging into node logs, many failures show `failed to attach network interface` from provider which correlates to AZ placement pressure.
maria: provider quotas in eu-west at soft-limit for spot-like instance types. autoscaler prefers spot to save cost; fallback path is to use on-demand node type. we can flip pool to fallback type temporarily.
kai: do it. fallback to on-demand-instance-type=c5d-like equivalent. estimate ~10 min to warm. also route 25% traffic to gpux-central fallback.

```
# switch pool instance type
infra update-pool-config --pool gpux-eu --instance-type on-demand-48g --reason "incident fallback"
route-config set-weight --pool gpux-central 0.25 --from-pool gpux-eu
```

maria: update accepted. autoscaler now provisioning on-demand nodes; some nodes still slow due to image startup, looks like the new image (v2026-03-06) has a startup race under heavy attach concurrency.

leo: note: recent image rollout included an extra systemd unit that waits on fsck, which can hang if cloud image attaches too quickly.
kai: can we revert image to last stable? if so do rolling pin.
maria: switching image to v2026-03-02 and restarting provisioner.

```
# image revert
infra update-pool-config --pool gpux-eu --image v2026-03-02
infra restart-provisioner --pool gpux-eu
```

jordan: autoscaler config tweak: reduce scale_down_stabilization to avoid oscillation later, bump scale_up_timeout to 7 minutes.
sara: after image revert and on-demand fallback, queue dropped from 920 -> 160 in ~12 minutes. 429s are down but some customers still see elevated latencies.
support-lead: posted status update: "Partial service interruption in eu-west affecting inference endpoints. Mitigation in progress." Top impacted customers notified.

kai: good work. monitoring for flapping. while we recover, put a soft-per-tenant cap to avoid a single tenant consuming >25% of new capacity.
maria: applied tenant soft caps. metrics show top-tenant share down from 48% -> 22%.

sara: small regression: after ~30m nodes started to register then a wave of placement failures hit again in a different AZ. suspect provider placement instability rather than our config. will open cloud support ticket.

ops-bot: Recommendation: migrate critical workloads to dedicated reserved hosts if provider instability persists.
kai: agree. schedule reserved host provisioning for gpux-eu if cloud doesn't stabilize in 2h.

--- INCIDENT MITIGATION SUMMARY ---
kai: declaring mitigated at 03:00 UTC; root mitigation was multi-step: enable burst-protection, switch fallback instance type to on-demand, revert problematic image, apply per-tenant soft caps, and shift fractional traffic to gpux-central.

Metrics: peak queue 932 at 02:56 UTC; impacted ~95 customers with degraded performance; 429/503 errors observed for ~23 minutes; top-5 tenants accounted for 60% of queued backlog.

Timeline (short):
- 02:48 UTC queue rise begins
- 02:50 UTC automated alerts & page to oncall
- 02:54 UTC burst-protection toggled; partial relief
- 02:58 UTC fallback instance type switch + route shift
- 03:06 UTC image revert to v2026-03-02
- 03:12 UTC queue trending down, mitigation holding
- 03:00-04:00 UTC monitoring window

Action items (owners / due):
- infra: add alert for provider placement errors aggregated by AZ and instance-type (maria, 1w)
- infra: add pre-promotion bootstrap test for AMIs that simulates high NIC attach concurrency (leo, 2w)
- runtime: implement autoscaler heuristic to prefer fallback instance-types earlier when CreateFailed rate > threshold (jordan, 3w)
- product: add automated status triggers for pool-level degradation and a customer visibility playbook (support-lead, 1w)
- ops: create runbook for reserved-host hot provisioning and add capacity gating to avoid cross-tenant hogging (kai, 2w)

Lessons:
- single image regressions interacting with provider placement can cascade into rapid queue growth; image boot-time regressions must be caught by pre-promotion stress tests.
- soft per-tenant caps + burst-protection are effective short-term mitigations and should be automated in the fallback playbook.
- autoscaler needs better signals for when to switch instance types vs retrying the same placement strategy.

support-lead: customer outreach complete; one enterprise customer requested a post-incident review call scheduled tomorrow.

maria: opened cloud ticket with provider referencing placement failures and network attach errors; attached provisioning logs.

kai: wrapping up. will create the formal postmortem doc with graphs and attach logs. assigning action items in tracker. thanks all. :pray: 

incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated at 6111113600. Monitoring until 6111117200.
